approval.cost: No listing or approval fee is stated on the official pages read. For Private Apps needing more calls, the FAQ says only: 'If you're building a Private app and think you need a higher API limit you should reach out to our sales team' (no price stated)
approval.trigger: Public Apps require approval before launching. Verbatim from the official comparison table: 'Requires approval before launching: Public Apps: Yes; Private Apps: No.' And: 'Public apps can be listed on SurveyMonkey's App Directory after meeting certain criteria and receiving approval.' You submit via the listings tab in My Apps ('Visit the listings tab in the My Apps view to create an app listing and submit it for approval'; first listing in English). The official App Approval Checklist states the criteria verbatim: 'Your app should have unique value and be attracting new users regularly'; 'Your app should NOT replicate functionality already offered by SurveyMonkey's survey tools'; 'Your app's name should NOT be a generic term (i.e. Analytics), include versioning (i.e. App V3.0), and/or include the word SurveyMonkey'; 'Your app should have at least five OAuth sign ins in the first three months'; 'You must state if users will need a free or paid account from your service to use your app'; 'Your team must provide easily-accessible app support'; 'All communication should be over HTTPS using a valid SSL certificate.' Discretion clause, verbatim: 'SurveyMonkey retains the right to reject an app based on criteria not listed above. Approval of your app by SurveyMonkey does not guarantee its compliance with the criteria above.' Caps: Public Apps have 'API call limits: 500,000/day' ('Limits are subject to change'); Private Apps start at '500 calls/day (contact sales)' to increase, and are hard-capped in reach to one SurveyMonkey account or one Team, with no App Directory eligibility.
approval.wait: Not stated (the official pages state no approval duration)

blockers.detail: A Private App can never serve outside customers (one account or one Team, no App Directory eligibility); a Public App cannot launch at all until SurveyMonkey approves it. Pick wrong and you rebuild/re-submit.
blockers.howToClear: Choose Public App at creation for any multi-customer product.
blockers.title: App-type choice is a one-way door in practice

blockers.detail: FAQ, verbatim: 'You can refresh your app's credential in the settings for your app in the developer portal. This will refresh your secret, revoking all access to your app.' Rotating the app secret revokes access for EVERY connected user at once; there is no per-user/per-token revocation described on the official pages read.
blockers.howToClear: Treat secret rotation as a break-glass, all-customers event with a re-authorization plan.
blockers.title: Revocation is coarse and all-or-nothing

blockers.detail: Approval is discretionary beyond the published checklist ('SurveyMonkey retains the right to reject an app based on criteria not listed above'), and apps replicating SurveyMonkey's own survey functionality are ineligible; the app name may not be generic, contain versioning, or include 'SurveyMonkey'. Approval also 'does not guarantee compliance', so listing risk persists after launch.
blockers.howToClear: Position the app as clearly additive value, name it distinctly, and keep meeting the checklist after launch.
blockers.title: Discretionary approval; no cloning or naming traps

alternatives: Private App (for a single account or one Team: internal automation, an organization automating its own surveys/data export). It requires no approval, but it cannot be offered to arbitrary outside customers and is not eligible for the App Directory; for Private Apps the DEVELOPER purchases the SurveyMonkey accounts
flavor.recommended: A Public App in the SurveyMonkey API Developer Portal, with OAuth sign-in by end users
flavor.why: The object is an App created in the SurveyMonkey API Developer Portal (developer.surveymonkey.com > My Apps). At creation you choose an app type: Public App or Private App. Per SurveyMonkey's official comparison table, Public Apps are the only type outside users can connect ('How many accounts can access the app: Unlimited', vs Private: 'One SurveyMonkey account or one Team'), and for Public Apps the 'SurveyMonkey account needs to be an enduser of the app', with the end user purchasing their own SurveyMonkey account. The Public App approval checklist confirms the connection mechanism is OAuth sign-in by end users: 'Your app should have at least five OAuth sign ins in the first three months.'

humanMust: Sign in to the SurveyMonkey Developer Portal and create the app in My Apps, choosing Public App
Configure the app and select the scopes it needs (the FAQ directs developers to the API Documentation for scopes)
Create the app listing in the listings tab (first listing in English) and submit it for approval
Provide easily-accessible app support and maintain at least five OAuth sign-ins in the first three months
name: SurveyMonkey
nuances: Economics differ by type: for Private Apps the developer purchases the SurveyMonkey accounts; for Public Apps the end user purchases their own account, so your customers need their own SurveyMonkey accounts (with a plan sufficient to be an end user of the app) to connect.

Call-limit asymmetry: a private/internal deployment starts at 500 calls/day, so polling-heavy designs hit the ceiling fast; the official private-app guidance recommends webhooks instead of polling, client-side caching, batching changes, and Bulk API endpoints to stay within limits. Public Apps get 500,000 calls/day.
All communication must be over HTTPS with a valid SSL certificate (an approval-checklist requirement, not just a recommendation).
prerequisites: A SurveyMonkey account for the Developer Portal
The Public vs Private app-type decision at creation

tagline: A Public App with OAuth sign-in, but SurveyMonkey must approve it before it can launch, against a published checklist (including at least five OAuth sign-ins in the first three months) plus an explicit right to reject for unlisted reasons.
